newsitem.title: USA: Damen to form bank holding company, sets buyback.
newsitem.headline: Damen to form bank holding company, sets buyback.

text.p: Damen Financial Corp, parent of $235.3 million-asset Damen Federal Bank, said Friday the Federal Reserve Bank approved its application to become a bank holding company.
The transaction is scheduled to be completed February 27, 1997, after completion of the regulatory waiting period, Damen said in a statement.
Damen also said its directors approved the repurchase of up to 850,000 shares or about 22.7 percent of the company's 3.75 million shares outstanding.
The shares will be repurchased after the bank holding company reorganization has been completed.

Damen said the repurchase will be made through a modified Dutch auction tender offer. Under this procedure, Damen shareholders can sell part or all of their shares to the company at an estimated price range of not less than $13.25 a share and not more than $14.75.

Based on these estimates, if 850,000 shares were bought, the total purchase price would range from about $11.3 million to $12.5 million, Damen said. The offer is expected to begin February 27, 1997 and expire March 26, 1997, unless extended.
If the number of shares tendered were greater than the number sought, Damen said it would select the lowest price that would allow it to buy the number of shares it seeks.

"Damen Financial intends to make the tender offer because its Board of Directors believes that the purchase of shares pursuant to the offer should have beneficial effects on stockholder value while maintaining a strong capital base to support the needs of our business and our customers," said Mary Beth Poronsky Stull, Damen's president and chief executive officer, in a statement.

"After studying a number of alternatives, we selected the Modified Dutch Auction Tender because it is a positive action that has the potential for improving stockholder returns in an expeditious manner," she said.
